messages:
Amir: Quick brain-dump: proposal for a minimal active/active fallback for region-constrained tenants. Primary rule: resident-region handles full read/write. If resident region is degraded, route to a consented cross-region 'guest-proxy' that enforces strict limits (stateless inference, tokenized inputs, no artifact writes). Thoughts?

Dina: Lean idea. Main concern: accidental cross-border data flow. Need an explicit signed consent token from control plane that lists allowed fallback regions and a TTL. Runtime must verify.

Amir: Exactly  control plane issues short-lived signed assertion (residency-assertion) enumerating permitted fallback targets and allowed features. Runtime rejects requests without it.

Mike: Ops note: do not underestimate load concentration. If many tenants fall back to same guest pool we risk saturation. Suggest per-tenant rate limits and an admission controller.

Sara: From product: preferable to expose a degraded-but-useful mode (e.g., limited-length outputs, disabled tools) instead of full blackout. Also customers must be able to opt-out of any cross-region fallback.

Leah: Legal: even read-only inference outside of a jurisdiction can trigger compliance issues. Must be explicit opt-in in contract, and surfaced in tenant settings.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: guest-proxy:v0.4 -> dedicated-escrow-pool @ 2024-06-14T04:00Z

Dina: RFC follow-up: propose HTTP headers for the contract: \"X-Residency-Mode: resident|guest\" and \"X-Residency-Assertion: <signed-jwt>\". Guardian: for guarded tenants, runtime returns 403 if assertion missing or invalid.

Amir: Local dev example:
```
curl -H "X-Residency-Assertion: eyJhbGciOi..." https://api.redwood/infer -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Mike: Telemetry we need: guest_fallback_count_total{tenant}, guest_fallback_p95_latency, guest_pool_queue_depth, and guest_admissions_rejected. Also add circuit-breaker heuristics: trip on >10% 5xx over 1m or tail latency > 2s.

Sara: :thumbsup: I'll add product EPIC "guest-proxy-fallback" and coordinate comms once infra agrees on metrics and CBs.

Leah: Also request: KMS key scoping rules for signing assertions and strict audit logs for any cross-region calls. Legal will prepare amendment language.

Dina: Edge case: model pinning. If tenant pinned to a specific heavy model absent from guest pool, runtime must consult a fallback-mapping table to map to compatible variants or return a controlled degraded response. Need mapping doc per model family.

Amir: Proposed action items:
- Dina: write short RFC for assertion format + runtime validation (due Mon)
- Mike: simulate fallback load and propose SLOs + admission strategy (due Wed)
- Sara: draft product opt-in settings and comms (due Tue)
- Leah: prepare contract addendum and KMS requirements (due Fri)
- Ops: proceed with canary (deploy-bot scheduled it)
Any blockers?

Mike: No blockers. I'll instrument metrics and prepare a Grafana template.

Sara: I'll create the EPIC and start a customer-facing FAQ draft.

Amir: Adding a snippet from the last chaos run showing guest fallbacks:
```
[2024-05-12T11:02:09Z] tenant=beta-corp fallback=guest-proxy region=us-west-2 rtt=130ms
[2024-05-12T11:02:10Z] tenant=beta-corp fallback=guest-proxy region=ap-southeast-1 rtt=220ms
```

Dina: One infra constraint: do not let guest pool share model weights across tenants. Enforce per-tenant ephemeral caches or strict namespace isolation for model artifacts.

Leah: Agreed. Legal asks for explicit \"no artifact distribution\" clause in the amendment.

Amir: Thanks everyone. I'll draft the RFC and ping this thread when ready. /cc @Dina @Mike @Sara @Leah
